text:
Predicates:
ListedInYelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
HasRatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x) ::: x receives many negative reviews.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
Store(x) ::: x is a store.
HamdenPlazaSubway(x) ::: x is the Hamden Plaza Subway store.
Rating(x, y) ::: x has rating y.

Premises:
∀x (ListedInYelp(x) → ¬ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4 → ListedInYelp(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Rating(HamdenPlazaSubway, y) ∧ y > 4 ∨ PopularAmongLocals(HamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
¬ProvidesTakeOut(HamdenPlazaSubway) ???
